video.title: He Gets These Free. Makes $1,000 With Each.

summary: Chris Koerner visits Kyler in Utah to show how he repairs free discarded dryers, then sells or rents them through Facebook Marketplace. Kyler describes rentals as recurring income and flipping as a separate source of active income, with delivery, installation and maintenance included for rentals. He also explains TakeMyAppliance, a website that connects appliance owners with people who want appliances to flip, rent or sell. The main takeaway is to test demand by listing early, then choose between a quicker sale and longer-term rental income.

ideas.name: Repair and flip discarded appliances
ideas.one_liner: Collect free or unwanted appliances, repair and clean them, then sell them as tested used appliances.
ideas.business_model: Buy or acquire appliances cheaply or for free, repair them, and sell each unit for a one-off price.
ideas.customer: People shopping for used appliances through Facebook Marketplace; specific buyer demographics are not stated.
ideas.problem: Buyers want a working appliance at a lower price than a new one; this customer need is implied by the listings, not directly described.
ideas.offer: A cleaned, tested, working dryer, with a 30-day guarantee and optional cable change.

pricing.model: One-off sale per appliance; price lower for a faster sale or higher if willing to wait.

Expected used-store price or a slower Marketplace sale
Host's general claim about used appliances sold by Kyler

pricing.notes: The host listed the demonstrated dryer at $175; Kyler said a lower price could sell it the same day.

acquisition_channels.details: Kyler and Chris created a Facebook Marketplace listing with photos, a title, condition, description and price. They also suggested sharing listings in local groups.
Supply comes from appliances left at the curb or owners wanting to get rid of them. Kyler also described TakeMyAppliance as a way to find appliance leads.

ideas.delivery: Collect the appliance, diagnose it, replace failed parts, clean lint and the exterior, test that it spins and heats, photograph and list it, then arrange sale and delivery. Kyler and Chris perform the repair and handling in the demonstration.
unit_economics_claims: Kyler says flipping appliances brings in $5,000 per month when rental demand is lower.
The demonstrated repair used low-cost parts, including a $20 kit and a $5 to $10 belt.
ideas.startup_cost: $300 per month for the garage was disclosed; total startup cost was not stated. Tools and example replacement parts are additional costs.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: A same-day sale is presented as possible at a lower price; no completed sale timeline is reported for the demonstrated dryer.

acquisition.how: Marketplace listings and inbound buyer messages can be templated, but sourcing local discarded units and managing messages still needs human attention. No unsolicited outreach is described.

onboarding.how: A listing can collect initial buyer questions, but confirming condition, cable needs and collection or delivery details requires human checks.

delivery.how: A person must collect, repair, clean, test and move the physical appliance.

billing.how: Payment is a one-off sale, but the transcript does not state the payment method or any automated payment setup.

support.how: Warranty questions and appliance faults require someone to assess and potentially repair the unit.

uk_applicability.notes: The used-appliance resale model could work in the UK, but it would need local sourcing, pricing and delivery arrangements. Electrical and product safety, consumer rights and waste rules would need to be handled for the UK.

risks: The fault is unknown until the unit is tested, so repair time and parts costs can vary.
Electrical and heating repairs carry safety risks; the video does not describe formal training or safety procedures.
Lint buildup can cause overheating, so cleaning and testing are important.
A low sale price may improve speed but reduce the return per unit.
AI-edited listing photos could misrepresent the appliance if they show a cable or condition the actual unit does not have.

ideas.name: Rent out repaired appliances
ideas.one_liner: Repair discarded appliances, rent them locally with delivery and maintenance, and collect recurring monthly payments.
ideas.business_model: Monthly appliance rental, with delivery, installation and maintenance included.
ideas.customer: Families whose dryer has broken and who want to keep doing laundry without buying a new dryer or using a laundromat.
ideas.problem: A broken dryer interrupts laundry; buying a replacement can be costly and using a laundromat takes time.
ideas.offer: A working dryer delivered and installed, with maintenance and a stated 30-day guarantee.

pricing.notes: Kyler says a renter may keep a unit for at least two years, but that is a projection, not a guaranteed term.

acquisition_channels.details: They created a separate Facebook Marketplace listing for the dryer as a rental, priced it at $45 per month, and suggested sharing it to local groups.

ideas.delivery: Clean and present the unit, load it onto a trailer, deliver it to the renter, install it, and provide maintenance if it breaks. Kyler and Chris handled the demonstrated delivery and installation.
unit_economics_claims: Kyler says he makes over $10,000 per month from appliance rentals.
Kyler projects that a renter paying $45 per month for two years would pay $1,080 in total.
Kyler says 90% of the time a delivery customer gives him their old dryer.
ideas.startup_cost: $300 per month for the garage was disclosed; total startup cost was not stated. The operator also needs appliances, repair parts, tools and delivery capacity.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: The demonstration received a rental inquiry about 40 minutes after the listings were posted. Payment timing and time to the first rental payment are not stated.

acquisition.how: A Marketplace listing can attract inbound enquiries and use an availability reply, but creating listings and handling renter questions still needs human review. No unsolicited outreach is described.

onboarding.how: Rental details and scheduling could be collected through forms, but confirming the unit, address, delivery access and installation needs a human.

delivery.how: A person must deliver and install the appliance and return for maintenance or repair.

billing.how: Monthly recurring billing could be handled by payment software, though the transcript does not say what billing system Kyler uses.

support.how: Faults, maintenance, collection and replacement require physical work.

uk_applicability.notes: The rental model could work in the UK with local inventory and delivery coverage. UK consumer, electrical safety and rental contract requirements would need to be addressed; the prices and market examples are from Utah.

risks: Rental income accumulates over time, so the projected $1,080 takes two years to collect at $45 per month.
The operator remains responsible for delivery, installation and maintenance.
Basement access and other delivery constraints can add substantial physical effort.
The claim that customers often return an old dryer is not a guaranteed supply source.
A longer rental term depends on continued customer use and successful collection of payments.

tactics.name: Use a post-fix-sell workflow
steps: Source a free or unwanted appliance.
Post a listing before repair to see whether a buyer or renter responds.
Diagnose and repair the appliance if demand looks promising.
Retest it, clean it and complete the sale or rental.

quote.text: The big secret about everything we did is we posted before we even fixed the thing. We didn't even know who it if it would work.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Diagnose common dryer failures with a multimeter
steps: Check whether the dryer powers on.
Remove the back panel and test the thermal fuse for continuity.
If it spins but does not heat, test the heating element.
Inspect the belt and roller wheels, remove lint, replace failed parts and retest.

quote.text: If it beeps, it's good, and I have no idea what's wrong. If it doesn't beep, we need a new one.
quote.speaker: Kyler

quote.text: We drove it about 15 minutes away, and sadly it was a basement apartment.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: The host and guest describe changing a repeated listing to get around Facebook's duplicate warning. Platform rules may restrict this approach.

quote.text: Okay, so we're going to trick Facebook. We'll get that. So, we'll do this. One item, add photos. We're going to go boom, boom, boom.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Test demand before spending more time on a repair: listing early can reveal interest while the unit is still being fixed.

quote.text: The big secret about everything we did is we posted before we even fixed the thing. We didn't even know who it if it would work.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Choose pricing based on the desired time to sale; a lower price may move inventory faster, while a higher price may require waiting.

quote.text: If you want to sell it the same day, I would price it more aggressively in the 140 to 150 range. That's normally what I do cuz I I do high volume a little bit lower price.
quote.speaker: Kyler

lessons.lesson: A single asset can be offered through different money models: a quick sale or a recurring rental.

quote.text: With this dryer, you could have sold it for $175, made some quick cash, or what's crazy is people all over the US will rent uh washers and dryers
quote.speaker: Kyler

lessons.lesson: Rental revenue can be recurring, but the total value of a long rental takes time to collect and depends on the customer staying.

quote.text: The asterisk is it it can take some time to collect all that money, but if we want money now, we sell for 175 same day.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Combining rentals with flipping gives the operator another way to earn when rental demand is lower.

quote.text: And I think the the flipping business and the rental business complement each other cuz there's not always crazy demand for the rentals and vice versa.
quote.speaker: Kyler

lessons.lesson: A specialized lead website can address an inconsistent supply problem that makes a local resale business harder to scale.

quote.text: Finding dryers and washers on the side of the road isn't the most consistent way. So, we built a website called TakeMyAppliance
quote.speaker: Kyler

lessons.lesson: For this kind of physical business, online listings can automate discovery, but repair, delivery and maintenance still depend on people.

evidence_quality.rationale: Kyler describes a first-hand operating process with concrete repair steps, listing tactics and reported revenue. The income, lead volume, customer-return rate and rental duration are self-reported and not independently verified; the demonstration is a single unit.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Chris Koerner promotes HighLevel with a referral URL and a free-trial offer during the video.
